core_obligations: Existence of the limiting object (proof lines 6072-6092): Z_inf, B_inf and hence E_inf are objects of the graded category by the construction of the spectral sequence; if the displayed intersections and unions of the degree p parts of Z_r and B_r exist, then Z_inf and B_inf exist with those degree p parts, by an elementary argument about unions and intersections of graded subobjects, and E_inf^p is the displayed quotient.
The comparison (proof lines 6094-6115): the two displayed inclusions identify the kernel of d in F^pK modulo the image of d in F^pK plus the next filtration step as a subquotient of E_inf^p.

Conclusion (proof lines 6115-6119): comparing that subquotient with the formula for gr^p H(K) from the definition of the filtration on the cohomology of a filtered differential object proves the second assertion.
proof_roadmap: Identify the degree p parts of the intersections and unions defining the limiting page.
Put the kernel over the image as a subquotient of the limiting page using the two inclusions.
Compare with the displayed description of the associated graded of the cohomology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that when the limiting terms of the spectral sequence of a filtered differential object exist, the limiting page is graded by Z_inf^p/B_inf^p and the associated graded of the cohomology is a graded subquotient of it (statement lines 6058-6069). The proof is a complete argument: the degree p parts of Z_inf and B_inf are identified as displayed intersections and unions, using the construction of the spectral sequence and an elementary argument about graded subobjects (proof lines 6072-6092); two displayed inclusions exhibit the kernel over the image as a subquotient of the limiting page (proof lines 6094-6115); and the comparison with the definition of the filtration on cohomology closes the argument (proof lines 6115-6119). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping with intersections and unions of graded subobjects. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
